plain: The claim is that a secret 1953 panel of scientists set the goal for the US Air Force's UFO study, Project Blue Book: to play down and explain away sightings. Michels tells it himself. He says the papers of the Robertson Panel, a group of scientists called together by the CIA, show that Blue Book's 'literal explicit motive' was to 'throw the public off and systematically downplay, suppress, and rationalize UFO sightings'. On the same show, crediting the physicist Hal Puthoff, he gives the reason as fear that the truth 'would touch off mass hysteria'. On another show he says the panel's head, the physicist Howard P. Robertson, 'created the Mandate for Blue Book', and dates it to 1952 and 1953. If he is right, the public face of the government's UFO work was meant from the start to steer people away. The other voice is the panel's report, dated 16 February 1953, from the CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence. It recommends a 'debunking' aim that 'would result in reduction in public interest in "flying saucers"'. Among the dangers it lists the 'Subjectivity of public to mass hysteria', and it warns of 'hostile propaganda' that could cause 'harmful distrust of duly constituted authority'. The report also lists 'Project BLUE BOOK' progress reports among the evidence the panel saw, so Blue Book was already running when it met. That the panel's aim was Blue Book's own motive, or that the panel created Blue Book's mandate, is Michels' step, which the report neither states nor rules out.

discussion.by: Report of Meetings of Scientific Advisory Panel on Unidentified Flying Objects (Robertson Panel), 14-18 January 1953
discussion.text: The tellers do not say which of the panel's papers they mean; in the minutes and the report read here the panel recommends a "debunking" aim that "would result in reduction in public interest in 'flying saucers'", names among the dangers the "Subjectivity of public to mass hysteria", and lists among the evidence it was shown the "ATIC Status and Progress Reports of Project GRUDGE and Project BLUE BOOK", so Blue Book was already running when the panel met. That the aim the panel set out was Blue Book's own motive, or that the panel created Blue Book's mandate, is the tellers' step, which the report neither states nor excludes.
